dedupe_keys.name: social life cycle assessment of infectious healthcare waste supply chains in latvia panacea project data

description: This data set scores the social effects of the two ways infectious waste from Latvian hospitals is handled, from the ward to final disposal. The producers are Julija Gusca and colleagues at Riga Technical University, in the Panacea project on circular economy approaches in healthcare waste management funded by the Latvian Council of Science. Coverage is two supply chains: waste from a university hospital sent to thermal treatment and then landfill, and waste from a regional hospital sent to chemical treatment and then energy recovery. Following the UN Environment Programme guidelines for social life cycle assessment, the workbooks give categories, sub-categories and indicators, with their weights and scores, for waste generation in hospitals, transport and treatment, and end of life; a PDF lists the indicators applied. The files are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, with the method and results in the Environmental and Climate Technologies article. Caveats: scores rest partly on survey and expert judgement, two chains only, and no waste quantities or costs are included. Simulation uses: adding social criteria to optimisation of healthcare waste treatment routes, and comparing centralised and regional treatment options. Related records: the Basel Convention national reporting data (data-basel-convention-national-reporting) cover hazardous waste flows, and SwolfPy (model-swolfpy) optimises waste management systems.
